meta.methodology: Heuristic scoring based on publicly available platform documentation and capability assessments
meta.disclaimer: Scores are indicative. Validate against your organisation's specific requirements and procurement facts.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI
strengths: Native Gemini model family with multimodal capabilities
Tight BigQuery integration for analytics and feature engineering
Managed vector search with low-latency retrieval
Best-in-class model evaluation and experiment tracking
Vertex AI Agent Builder for rapid agent prototyping
Unified ML platform from training to serving
Strong Kubernetes ecosystem via GKE for custom workloads
weaknesses: Smaller enterprise footprint than Azure in regulated industries
Fewer pre-built enterprise connectors compared to Microsoft ecosystem
Less entrenched in legacy enterprise procurement channels

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI
strengths: Deepest enterprise integration via Microsoft 365 and Azure AD
Industry-leading compliance certifications for regulated sectors
Content safety and responsible AI guardrails built-in
Azure AI Search with hybrid retrieval capabilities
Strong enterprise procurement and support channels
Seamless Active Directory and identity integration
Copilot Studio for low-code agent building
weaknesses: Less flexibility for model experimentation outside OpenAI family
Azure AI Search can be expensive at scale
Vendor lock-in to Microsoft ecosystem is significant
Model evaluation tooling less mature than Vertex AI

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
strengths: Broadest model marketplace with Claude, Llama, Mistral, Titan, and more
Deep AWS infrastructure control and customization
Strong IAM and VPC integration for security
Bedrock Agents for workflow orchestration
SageMaker integration for custom model training
Largest cloud infrastructure footprint globally
Knowledge Bases for managed RAG pipelines
weaknesses: Developer UX more fragmented across multiple services
Tooling spread across Bedrock, SageMaker, and other services
Model evaluation and experiment tracking less unified
Cost predictability harder due to service sprawl
platforms.pricing_model: Pay-per-token with on-demand and provisioned throughput

platforms.name: Claude Computer Use
strengths: Most advanced multi-step reasoning for complex desktop and browser tasks
Native screenshot understanding with pixel-level accuracy
Built-in safety guardrails and human-in-loop confirmation gates
Handles arbitrary GUI interactions (clicks, typing, navigation)
Strong constitutional AI alignment reduces rogue agent behavior
Deepest research and data-extraction capabilities
Enterprise API with audit logging and usage controls
weaknesses: Highest cost per completed task among computer-use agents
Slower execution due to deliberative reasoning at each step
Requires Anthropic API — no self-hosted option
Limited browser automation compared to dedicated browser agents
platforms.pricing_model: Per-token with tool-use surcharge per action

platforms.name: Browserbase
strengths: Purpose-built cloud browser infrastructure for agent automation
Lowest cost per task for web scraping and data extraction
API-first design with Playwright/Puppeteer compatibility
Managed browser sessions with anti-detection and proxy support
Excellent horizontal scaling for parallel task execution
Session recording and replay for debugging
Stealth mode for sites with bot-detection
weaknesses: Limited to browser-based tasks — no desktop automation
No native AI reasoning — relies on external LLM providers
Enterprise governance features still maturing
Human-in-loop capabilities are basic

platforms.name: Manus AI
strengths: Broadest autonomous task execution across browser and desktop
End-to-end task completion without hand-holding
Built-in planning and self-correction capabilities
Handles multi-application workflows (browser + files + APIs)
Good natural language task specification
Growing ecosystem of pre-built task templates
weaknesses: Newer platform with less enterprise track record
IT approvability is challenging — limited compliance certifications
Opaque execution model — harder to audit intermediate steps
Security posture not yet validated for regulated environments
Limited enterprise SSO and RBAC integration

platforms.name: Replit Agent
strengths: Best-in-class code generation with immediate execution environment
Integrated deployment — goes from idea to live app in one tool
Natural language to full-stack application generation
Built-in environment management (packages, DBs, secrets)
Excellent for rapid prototyping and MVP building
Good cost efficiency for development-focused tasks
weaknesses: Focused on code/dev tasks — limited browser automation
Not designed for enterprise data-entry or form-fill workflows
Limited compliance certifications for regulated industries
Governance and audit trail capabilities are minimal
Less reliable for complex multi-step non-coding tasks

platforms.name: Cursor AI
strengths: Best IDE-integrated AI agent with deep codebase understanding
Multi-file editing with context-aware code generation
Excellent reliability for code-centric multi-step tasks
Human-in-loop review at each code change with diff preview
Supports multiple LLM backends (GPT-4, Claude, Gemini)
Strong privacy controls — code stays local by default
weaknesses: IDE-bound — no browser or desktop automation capabilities
Not suitable for data-entry, form-fill, or web scraping
Enterprise governance features are limited
No compliance certifications beyond basic SOC 2
Single-user focused — limited team coordination features
platforms.pricing_model: Monthly subscription with request-based usage tiers
